newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group withdraws Evergreen protest.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group withdraws Evergreen protest.

text.p: New York consumer and civil rights group Inner City Press/Community on the Move said Wednesday it was withdrawing a petition filed with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission against Evergreen Media Corp.
The petition sought to block their acquisition of two radio stations from Viacom Inc.
Inner City said it reached agreement with Evergreen "to further improve their service and treatment of the low income community of color in New York."

Inner City said that under the deal, Evergreen agreed to expand recruitment of Hispanic and black employees, produce a new public affairs program aimed at the minority community, increase public service announcements of interest to that community, and make discounted radio advertising available to minority businesses.

In February, Evergreen announced it was buying Chancellor Broadcasting Co for about $1.5 billion in stock and debt. Chancellor owns 51 radio stations in 15 metropolitan U.S. markets. Evergreen in February also agreed to buy Viacom's radio station group for $1.075 billion.
Matthew Lee, executive director of Inner City, said the agreement "resolves the issues we raised in our petition to deny the merger."
An Evergreen spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
